title: Annotatio III §.VII open: Transsubstantiation’s monster thrust into public light — still unnamed; seated by papal decrees
pass_a_gloss: §. VII. The horrible monster of Transsubstantiation having by this means been thrust forth into public light (to which nonetheless all light was still taken away, because only after some space of time at last it saw itself adorned with its own proper name) was by Decrees of the highest Popes, pronouncing even from the Roman See of Peter itself, placed and established firmly enough upon a throne.
pass_b_english: §.VII: by this path the horrible Transsubstantiation-monster is thrust into public light — yet still without its proper name.
Papal decrees from Peter’s Roman seat plant it firmly enough on a throne.
source_text: §. VII. Protruso hac ratione in publicam lucem Transsubstantiationis monstro horrendo (cui lumen tamen ademtum adhuc omne erat, quòd post aliquod demum temporis spatium, nomine tandem suo proprio se exornatum vidit) Decretis summorum Paparum, ex ipsa etiam Romana Petri sede pronuntiantium, in thronum firmiter satis collocatum stabilitumque est.
